Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The present petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/-
alongwith interest @ 24% per annum from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its
realization being legal representatives of deceased Deepak(aged about 25 years), who died in road
traffic accident in question which occurred on 24.09.2020.

The petitioners also prayed for
compensation for irreparable monetary loss, mental agony, loss of love and affection and future
prospects plus all other heads of compensation as per entitlement, caused due to accidental death of
deceased who was their only son.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on
24.09.2020, deceased Deepak was going on his motorcycle bearing registration no. Dl8S-Bk-0483.

At about 8:29 Pm, when Macp No. 150/21; Fir No. 439/20; Ps. Alipur Dod: 07.06.2024 he
reached at Jhangola Road, Near Palla Village, Delhi, one motorcycle bearing registration no.
Dl11-Sb-5796 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein) at a
very high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against the aforesaid motorcycle of
the deceased, as a result of which, he fell down and sustained injuries.

He was immediately taken to
Bjrm Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi, where he was medically examined and declared 'brought
dead'.

Postmortem of the deceased was conducted at the mortuary of Bjrm Hospital, Jahangir Puri,
Delhi.

A case U/s 279/337/304A Ipc was registered at Ps. Alipur vide Fir No. 439/20 with regard
to the accident in question.

The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to
rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by
respondent no.1/driver.

The offending vehicle is claimed to be owned by respondent no.
2/registered owner namely Sh. Jal Bharat and the same was not insured at the time of accident.
According to Dar, the offending vehicle was found to be uninsured at the time of accident.

3. Although, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner put their appearance before
this Tribunal at the time of filing of Dar on 05.04.2021 but they failed to file their written statement
despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities.

Ultimately, their defence was struck off vide order
dated 20.12.2021.
Macp No. 150/21; Fir No. 439/20; Ps. Alipur Dod: 07.06.2024

4. In support of their claim, the petitioners have examined three witnesses i.e. Sh. Bittu Singh(father
of deceased) as Pw1, Pw2 Sh. Bablu (alleged eyewitness) and Pw3 Smt. Chhinder Kaur(mother of
deceased) and their evidence was closed vide order dated 14.03.2024.
5. Ld.

Counsel for petitioners/Lrs of deceased was heard at length and the record was perused
carefully.

(widow of deceased) is relevant.

Pw2 has deposed in his evidence that on 24.09.2020, the deceased
was going on his motorcycle bearing registration no. Dl8S-Bk-0483 Passion Pro and when the
deceased reached near Palla Village Jhangola Road, Delhi, suddenly offending motorcycle bearing

The ocular testimony of aforesaid witness remained unchallanged and uncontroverted from the side of respondents, who preferred not to contest the petition and stayed away from the proceedings.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW2, made on oath.
8. Moreover, the ocular testimony of PW2 is also corroborated by documentary evidence brought on record.
FIR No. 439/20 was registered at PS. Alipur with regard to accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on 25.09.2020 on the basis of GD Entry No. 0094A with regard to accident call received in PS. Alipur on 24.09.2020.
Copy of said FIR alongwith copy of chargesheet (which are part of criminal case record) would show that FIR was registered on the date of accident itself i.e. 24.09.2020.
Thus, FIR was registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondents and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner.
9. The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the criminal case, have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

Respondent no. 1 namely JCL Dharambir has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s. 279/304A IPC &
3/181, 5/181 & 185 M.V. Act by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried MACP No. 150/21; FIR No. 439/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 07.06.2024 out by it that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
Copy of said charge-sheet, which carries presumption of genuineness of its contents as provided in Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008.

10. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

sentences.text: The rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle may be proved, either by direct evidence or by circumstances including principle of res-ipsa loquitur.
It also an admitted fact that the respondent no. 1 was arrested in this case.

Furthermore, copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR),
would show that same was registered on the same day and on visit of the MACP No. 150/21; FIR No.
439/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 07.06.2024 police official at the spot, both the vehicles i.e. offending vehicle and vehicle of victim/deceased were found by him in accidental condition at the spot.

Both i.e. offending vehicle as well as vehicle of deceased are shown to have been seized by the police from the place of accident, as per copies of their respective seizure memos (which are also part of DAR).
Same would show that the accident occurred between the aforesaid two vehicles at the time of accident.
It is also an undisputed fact that FIR No. 439/20 u/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS. Alipur with regard to accident in question.
12. Not only this, postmortem was got conducted on the body of deceased Deepak.

The copy of PM Report (which is part of DAR) of deceased, would show that cause of death of deceased was combined effect of head injury and hemorrhagic shock due to multiple bony injuries produced by blunt force impact.
The external injuries as mentioned in the relevant column correspond with the injuries which occur in Motor Vehicular Accident.
These documents have not been disputed from the side of respondents.

13. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderence of probabilities that Sh. Deepak had sustained fatal injuries in road accident which took place on 24.09.2020 at 8:30 PM at Gali No.
8, Part I, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle MACP No. 150/21; FIR No.
439/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 07.06.2024 bearing registration no. DL11-SB-5796 by respondent no.1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
14. The petitioners who are claimants are the parents of deceased.
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of their only son Deepak.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

15. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.

Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."
16. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.

By way of pronouncement of Pranay Sethi case (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has been pleased to hold that there shall be an increase of 10% on account of 'inflation' after a period of three years.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.
Reliance placed on Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd. V.
Kamlesh & Ors, MAC APP. No. 530/2008 passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court on 11.11.2008.
Bittoo Singh And Others (Lrs Of Deepak) vs Jcl Dharambir on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100304159/
3 11.
The rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle may be proved, either by direct evidence or by circumstances including principle of res-ipsa loquitur.
14. The petitioners who are claimants are the parents of deceased.
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of their only son Deepak.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.
15. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.
In Sarla Verma Bittoo Singh And Others (Lrs Of Deepak) vs Jcl Dharambir on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100304159/
4 & Ors.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
The aforesaid Principle of law has also been reiterated by a landmark judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme court in 2017 (13) SCALE 12 : 2017 XI AD (SC) 113 titled National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.
Accordingly, the quantum of appropriate and adequate compensation to the victim of road accident is to be derived after assessment of various relevant parameters, as per law.
Hence, the multiplier of 18 would be applicable in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC.
22.
Considering the age of deceased and the fact that he was not having permanent job at that time,
future prospects @ 40% has to be awarded in favour of petitioners in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors."
Alipur DOD: 07.06.2024 31.10.2017, as well as in view of decision of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in appeal bearing MAC APP No. 798/2011 titled as "Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pooja & Ors", decided on 02.11.17.
In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as, Pranay Sethi case (supra), the Tribunal considers that both the petitioners i.e. parents of deceased are entitled for payment of Rs. 40,000/- each towards "loss of consortium".
(Reliance placed on United India Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Baby Raksha & Ors, MAC APP. No. 36/2023 passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court on 21.04.2023).

19. During the course of arguments, Ld. counsel for petitioners fairly conceded that for want of any cogent and definite evidence being led by petitioners regarding monthly income of deceased, his income may be considered as per Minimum Wages Act in order to calculate the loss of dependency.
He has further prayed that future prospects be also awarded to the petitioners as deceased had promising future.
